narrative.overview:
Meridian looks like the news apps its reader already trusts (BBC News, the NYT app, The Hindu app) and does not try to be cleverer than them. Bold serif headlines sit inside a clean, modern app layout: a white day ground or a near-black night ground, neutral greys with no tint, black and white ink, and one crimson accent. Each edition is finite, read from top to bottom, and ends with "You're all caught up".

The density is a news app's density: every headline gets a picture and a 3–4 line summary. Hairlines separate the stories, and a heavy 2px ink rule opens each section. Nothing is decorative unless it helps the reader find their way. The editorial voice comes from the serif and from restraint, never from ornament. The replaced "survey sheet" world (neatline, legend tints, grey-blue night) is gone and none of its apparatus comes back.

On a phone the page is one column with a full-bleed lead photo. On desktop it becomes a 7:5 lead-and-rows split, with the same components throughout.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds with real contrast: pure white, and near-black (#111) with neutral greys.
One crimson accent, used only in its listed roles.
Source Serif 4 bold for headlines and reading text. Schibsted Grotesk for every UI string.
Solid pill tabs, hairline rows, softly rounded photos.
Photos are shown at their own shape. The large ones are never cropped to a house ratio.
Read state is a drawn tick. A card is never dimmed.

rules.name: The One Crimson Rule
rules.body: The accent appears only in its listed roles: the section label in meta, Developing, links in running text, key-fact bullets, the active tab, the Latest badge, and focus, caret and selection. It never appears on headlines, rules, backgrounds or icons beyond these.

rules.name: The White-On-Fill Rule
rules.body: White text sits only on accent-fill, never on the text accent. At night the text accent is too light to carry white.

rules.name: The No-Tint Rule
rules.body: The greys are true neutrals (R = G = B). The night ground is #111, not a blue-grey. Sections are not colour-coded. Left and right politics are never coloured: the leaning scale is ink on rule-strong.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks, Sans Serves Rule
rules.body: Headlines and anything you read as prose are serif. Every control, label and count is Grotesk. Neither family crosses over.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a headline. The section label lives in the meta line under the summary on cards, and first in the meta line on articles.

rules.name: The Own-Shape Rule
rules.body: Large pictures (lead, feature, article hero) take the aspect-ratio class nearest the photo's own shape: 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 or 2:1. Portrait and square photos use 4:3, and photos of unknown size use 16:9. A share image with a masthead burned in is shown whole. Only thumbnails are a fixed 4:3 crop.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: Story cards are never raised, boxed or filled. A hairline separates them and the photo carries the weight.

dos: Do put every headline with a picture: a thumbnail for rows, or a ratio-matched photo for the lead and features.
Do choose large-picture ratios with `ratioClass()` (r43 / r32 / r169 / r21), so photos keep their own shape.
Do keep the accent in its listed roles, and put white text only on accent-fill.
Do separate stories with 1px rule hairlines, and open sections with a 2px ink rule.
Do use the leading-dot plus clip-path meta list. Every item carries its own `::before` dot.
Do choose the desktop section grid so that no card is orphaned: 3 or 4 rows beside the feature, then 3 or 2 columns.
Do keep every control a pill or circle at a 36–44px tap height.
donts: Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headlines.
Don't colour left/right politics, or colour-code sections.
Don't dim, grey or desaturate read cards. Read state is the tick.
Don't add inline `style=""` attributes (the CSP forbids them).
Don't use the crimson outside its listed roles: not on headlines, rules, backgrounds or decorative icons.
Don't tint the greys or move the night ground toward blue-grey.
Don't crop large pictures to a house ratio.
Don't bring back neatlines, legend keys or other ornament that does not help the reader find their way.
